# What Changed in Dimorphos’s Orbit After DART

Before the impact, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit the larger asteroid Didymos. Immediately afterward, its orbital period had shortened by 32 minutes and 42 seconds, to 11 hours, 22 minutes and 37 seconds.

Over the following weeks, Dimorphos lost more rocky material to space, while its orbital period continued to shorten. It eventually settled at 11 hours, 22 minutes and 3 seconds—a duration reported as 33 minutes and 15 seconds shorter than before impact. The orbit was no longer circular after the impact.
